$comment: Caller and authentication contract for every deployable Edge Function.
WHY THIS EXISTS: CI deploys every function with --no-verify-jwt, so the
Supabase gateway performs NO authentication. Each function's in-function
check IS the security boundary. That boundary is distributed across 27
entrypoints, so it can drift silently. This manifest makes it explicit and
machine-checked.
It is enforced by scripts/check-edge-function-auth.mjs (npm run check:edge-auth),
which fails when a deployable function is missing or unclassified, and which
recomputes originPolicy / serviceRole / configToml / authPrimitives from the
actual sources so an entry cannot silently lie about the code it describes.
The guard also follows each required primitive's VERDICT: its result must
reach an if-guard that returns or throws (directly, via a captured variable,
or via a named helper that returns it to a guarded call site). A call whose
result is discarded, or a guard that no longer exits, fails the build even
though the primitive is still "referenced". A family may list a primitive in
flowOnlyPrimitives when its verdict is enforced by something other than an
early exit — buildAllowedOrigins is the one case: its output becomes CORS
headers, and the browser (plus the Vary: Origin contract proven in
authContracts.test.ts) does the refusing.
Adding a function? Add it here in the same commit, or the guard fails.

webhook-bearer.description: Authorization: Bearer <WEBHOOK_SECRET>. Called by Postgres triggers via pg_net and by scheduled cron jobs, never by a browser.
webhook-bearer.emptySecretRationale: Each function either returns 500 when WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset, or guards the comparison with !!WEBHOOK_SECRET. isAuthorizedWebhook additionally compares against the literal 'Bearer ' + secret, so an empty secret cannot match an empty header.

webhook-bearer-or-internal-secret.description: Either Authorization: Bearer <WEBHOOK_SECRET> (trigger/cron) or x-internal-secret: <SEND_INTERNAL_SECRET> (service-role caller, i.e. another Edge Function).
webhook-bearer-or-internal-secret.emptySecretRationale: timingSafeEqualHeader returns false when either side is missing or empty, so an unset SEND_INTERNAL_SECRET cannot be matched by an empty header. The bearer branch is guarded by !!WEBHOOK_SECRET.

webhook-bearer-or-staff-jwt.description: Either Authorization: Bearer <WEBHOOK_SECRET> (cron) or a staff user's Supabase JWT verified by auth.getUser() then gated on the is_staff() RPC.
webhook-bearer-or-staff-jwt.emptySecretRationale: The bearer branch is guarded by !!WEBHOOK_SECRET; when it is unset the request falls through to the staff-JWT branch rather than being admitted.

staff-jwt.description: The staff member's own Supabase session JWT, verified against GoTrue via auth.getUser(), then authorised by the is_staff() RPC executed under that same user token.
staff-jwt.emptySecretRationale: No shared secret is involved. Authorisation is delegated to Supabase Auth and to is_staff(), which is evaluated under the caller's own token so a forged client cannot assert staff status.

staff-jwt-or-internal-secret.description: Either a staff JWT (auth.getUser() + is_staff()) or x-internal-secret: <SEND_INTERNAL_SECRET> for service-role callers such as pg_net triggers and sibling Edge Functions.
staff-jwt-or-internal-secret.emptySecretRationale: timingSafeEqualHeader returns false when the expected secret is empty, so an unset SEND_INTERNAL_SECRET closes the service path instead of opening it.

internal-secret.description: x-internal-secret: <SEND_INTERNAL_SECRET> only. No browser path. Trusted service-to-service callers.
internal-secret.emptySecretRationale: timingSafeEqualHeader returns false when either side is missing or empty.

agent-secret.description: x-agent-secret: <AGENT_CALLBACK_SECRET>. Only the SQL trigger and whatsapp-generate-reply hold this secret; it is never exposed to a browser.
agent-secret.emptySecretRationale: timingSafeEqualHeader returns false when either side is missing or empty.

meta-signature.description: Meta-originated request authenticated by an HMAC-SHA256 X-Hub-Signature-256 over the raw body using META_APP_SECRET, and/or the hub.verify_token handshake.
meta-signature.emptySecretRationale: See each function's emptySecretBehaviour. whatsapp-webhook treats an unset META_APP_SECRET as a failed signature and refuses to process. whatsapp-flow-endpoint deliberately degrades to RSA-envelope + flow_token session auth when META_APP_SECRET is unset; this is documented, not accidental.

feed-token.description: Opaque bearer token from calendar_feed_tokens, supplied as a query parameter. Calendar clients (Apple, Google, Outlook) cannot carry JWTs.
feed-token.emptySecretRationale: validateFeedToken returns null for an empty token, for an unknown token, for is_active = false and for an expired token. Every null path returns 401.

public-rate-limited.description: Deliberately unauthenticated pre-auth endpoint. There is no caller identity to check, so the controls are an origin allowlist, a per-IP rate limit and a global rate limit. Any function in this family MUST NOT expose customer data beyond a boolean-shaped answer.
public-rate-limited.emptySecretRationale: No secret participates in the caller check. Abuse is bounded by rate limiting rather than rejected by authentication, so these functions are held to the additional data-exposure rule above.

apply-customer-confirm.caller: whatsapp-agent and the confirmation button handler, service-to-service
apply-customer-confirm.replayDefence: none — idempotency is enforced downstream by booking state, not by the transport
apply-customer-confirm.emptySecretBehaviour: closed — timingSafeEqualHeader rejects when the expected secret is empty
apply-customer-confirm.notes: Applies a customer confirmation. The autonomous path writes state='confirmed' and deliberately bypasses is_staff(); the x-internal-secret check is therefore the only caller gate. index.ts is a serve() shim; the handler and its gate live in handler.ts so handler.test.ts can drive them as a function.

broadcast-message.replayDefence: none — a repeated broadcast is a staff-visible action, not a silent privilege escalation
broadcast-message.unauthorizedResponse: 401 Unauthorized (missing or invalid token), 403 Forbidden (authenticated but not staff)
broadcast-message.notes: Sends a message to many recipients.

calendar-feed.caller: external calendar clients (Apple Calendar, Google Calendar, Outlook)
calendar-feed.role: customer or staff, determined by the token's feed_type
calendar-feed.replayDefence: none by design — a subscription URL is fetched repeatedly; the token is revocable via is_active and expires_at
calendar-feed.emptySecretBehaviour: closed — validateFeedToken returns null for an empty token
calendar-feed.notes: Token travels in the URL, so it appears in client logs. Revocation is via calendar_feed_tokens.is_active. index.ts is a serve() shim; the handler and its token gate live in handler.ts so handler.test.ts can drive them as a function.

calendar-ics.role: customer or staff, determined by the token's feed_type
calendar-ics.unauthorizedResponse: 401 Unauthorized (invalid token), 403 Forbidden (valid token requesting another owner's booking)
calendar-ics.emptySecretBehaviour: closed — validateFeedToken returns null for an empty token
calendar-ics.notes: Adds a per-booking ownership check on top of token validation, which calendar-feed does not need. index.ts is a serve() shim; the token and ownership gates live in the exported handler so handler.test.ts can drive them as a function.

customer-phone-on-file.caller: customer portal login page, before any session exists
customer-phone-on-file.replayDefence: per-IP rate limit (5/60s) plus a global cap (200/60s) that survives IP rotation
customer-phone-on-file.notes: Unauthenticated by necessity: it answers whether a number is on file so the login page can choose password vs SMS code. That makes it an enumeration oracle, which is why the global cap exists alongside the per-IP one. Returns only two booleans. index.ts is a serve() shim; the gates live in the exported handler so handler.test.ts can drive them as a function.

dashboard-summary.unauthorizedResponse: 401 missing authorization / invalid token, 403 not staff
dashboard-summary.notes: Read-only aggregate. Returns 500 rather than allowing the request when the is_staff() RPC itself errors.

notify-booking-cancelled.replayDefence: none at the transport; duplicate sends are bounded by booking state
notify-booking-cancelled.unauthorizedResponse: 401 Unauthorized, or 500 when WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset
notify-booking-cancelled.emptySecretBehaviour: closed — returns 500 before evaluating the header when WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset

notify-booking-confirmed.replayDefence: none at the transport; duplicate sends are bounded by booking state
notify-booking-confirmed.unauthorizedResponse: 401 Unauthorized, or 500 when WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset
notify-booking-confirmed.emptySecretBehaviour: closed — returns 500 before evaluating the header when WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset
notify-booking-confirmed.notes: Calls whatsapp-send onward with the service-role JWT plus x-internal-secret.

notify-booking-ready.replayDefence: none at the transport; duplicate sends are bounded by booking state
notify-booking-ready.unauthorizedResponse: 401 Unauthorized, or 500 when WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset
notify-booking-ready.emptySecretBehaviour: closed — returns 500 before evaluating the header when WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset

notify-booking-reminder.caller: cron via pg_net, and the staff dashboard's Tomorrow's reminders panel
notify-booking-reminder.replayDefence: none at the transport; the staff path targets a single booking_id
notify-booking-reminder.unauthorizedResponse: 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden when authenticated but not staff
notify-booking-reminder.emptySecretBehaviour: closed — an unset WEBHOOK_SECRET falls through to the staff-JWT branch rather than admitting the request
notify-booking-reminder.notes: The staff path exists so the browser never needs WEBHOOK_SECRET.

notify-customer-welcome.caller: Postgres trigger via pg_net, or a service-role Edge Function
notify-customer-welcome.emptySecretBehaviour: closed — the bearer branch is guarded by WEBHOOK_SECRET being set and the internal branch by timingSafeEqualHeader
notify-customer-welcome.notes: Skips the getUser() call when the credential is a webhook or service bearer rather than a user JWT.

notify-staff.caller: AFTER INSERT triggers on booking_events, whatsapp_messages, salon_todos and waitlist_entries, via pg_net
notify-staff.emptySecretBehaviour: closed — !!WEBHOOK_SECRET guards the bearer branch; timingSafeEqualHeader guards the internal branch
notify-staff.notes: Staff Web Push fan-out, dark-launched behind STAFF_PUSH_ENABLED. Returns 500 when VAPID keys are absent rather than sending unsigned pushes.

notify-waitlist-joined.unauthorizedResponse: 401 Unauthorized, or 500 when WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset
notify-waitlist-joined.emptySecretBehaviour: closed — returns 500 before evaluating the header when WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset

postcode-lookup.caller: customer onboarding address step, which may run before a session exists
postcode-lookup.replayDefence: per-IP rate limit (8/60s) plus a global cap
postcode-lookup.unauthorizedResponse: 400 invalid postcode, 429 rate-limited, 500 when APITIER_API_KEY is unset, 502 on upstream failure
postcode-lookup.emptySecretBehaviour: closed for the upstream call — returns 500 rather than calling APITier without a key. The caller check itself uses no secret.
postcode-lookup.notes: Proxies a paid per-lookup API, so rate limiting protects spend as well as data. Returns only public Royal Mail PAF address data, never customer records.

reminder-send.caller: staff dashboard browser, or a service-role Edge Function
reminder-send.unauthorizedResponse: 401 missing authorization / invalid token, 403 not staff
reminder-send.emptySecretBehaviour: closed — timingSafeEqualHeader rejects when SEND_INTERNAL_SECRET is empty, leaving only the staff path
reminder-send.notes: Checks the internal secret first so service callers never pay for a getUser() round trip.

reminder-sms-fallback.emptySecretBehaviour: closed — the guard is !WEBHOOK_SECRET || !isAuthorizedWebhook(...), so an unset secret rejects
reminder-sms-fallback.notes: Sends SMS when a WhatsApp reminder could not be delivered.

resend-booking-notification.replayDefence: none — resending is the explicit purpose of the endpoint
resend-booking-notification.unauthorizedResponse: 401 Unauthorized, 403 when authenticated but not staff
resend-booking-notification.emptySecretBehaviour: closed for the onward call — returns 500 when WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset, because it re-invokes a notify-* function with that bearer
resend-booking-notification.notes: Holds WEBHOOK_SECRET only to authenticate its onward call, never to authenticate its own caller.

sms-send.caller: staff dashboard browser, or a service-role Edge Function such as reminder-sms-fallback
sms-send.unauthorizedResponse: 401 missing authorization / invalid token, 403 not staff
sms-send.emptySecretBehaviour: closed — timingSafeEqualHeader rejects when SEND_INTERNAL_SECRET is empty
sms-send.notes: Spends Twilio credit, so an auth regression here has a direct financial cost.

whatsapp-admin.emptySecretBehaviour: closed — timingSafeEqualHeader rejects when the expected secret is empty

whatsapp-agent.caller: the SQL trigger on inbound WhatsApp messages, and whatsapp-generate-reply
whatsapp-agent.replayDefence: none at the transport; the agent is additionally gated by AI_ASSISTANT_ENABLED and per-intent auto-send rules
whatsapp-agent.emptySecretBehaviour: closed — timingSafeEqualHeader rejects when AGENT_CALLBACK_SECRET is empty
whatsapp-agent.notes: index.ts is a shim that only calls serve(handleAgentRequest); the auth check lives in handler.ts so the dispatch contract stays importable under deno test. Never exposed to a browser — whatsapp-generate-reply exists precisely so staff never hold this secret.

whatsapp-flow-endpoint.replayDefence: RSA-encrypted request envelope plus a flow_token session lookup, in addition to the HMAC signature
whatsapp-flow-endpoint.unauthorizedResponse: 401 missing signature / invalid signature, 400 bad request
whatsapp-flow-endpoint.emptySecretBehaviour: degraded by design — when META_APP_SECRET is unset the signature check is skipped and the RSA envelope plus flow_token session lookup become the sole auth. Documented in-source as AUDIT-4.
whatsapp-flow-endpoint.notes: When META_APP_SECRET IS set, a missing X-Hub-Signature-256 header is rejected too, so omitting the header cannot skip the HMAC check.

whatsapp-generate-reply.replayDefence: none — suggest-only, nothing is sent or persisted
whatsapp-generate-reply.unauthorizedResponse: 401 missing authorization / invalid token, 403 not staff
whatsapp-generate-reply.emptySecretBehaviour: closed for the onward call — returns an explicit error when AGENT_CALLBACK_SECRET is unset rather than calling whatsapp-agent unauthenticated
whatsapp-generate-reply.notes: The staff-facing bridge to whatsapp-agent. It holds AGENT_CALLBACK_SECRET for its onward call only; the browser never sees it.

whatsapp-media.caller: Postgres trigger via pg_net, or a service-role Edge Function
whatsapp-media.replayDefence: none at the transport; a force flag makes re-fetching explicit
whatsapp-media.emptySecretBehaviour: closed — !!WEBHOOK_SECRET guards the bearer branch; timingSafeEqualHeader guards the internal branch
whatsapp-media.notes: Returns 500 when META_ACCESS_TOKEN is unset rather than attempting an unauthenticated Meta fetch.

whatsapp-register.emptySecretBehaviour: closed — timingSafeEqualHeader rejects when the expected secret is empty
whatsapp-register.notes: The only deployable function that never constructs a Supabase client.

whatsapp-send.caller: staff dashboard browser, plus every notify-* function and pg_net trigger
whatsapp-send.unauthorizedResponse: 401 missing authorization / invalid token, 403 not staff
whatsapp-send.emptySecretBehaviour: closed — timingSafeEqualHeader rejects when SEND_INTERNAL_SECRET is empty
whatsapp-send.notes: The busiest send path. Verifies the JWT via auth.getUser() against GoTrue rather than decoding it locally, so all signing algorithms are supported.

whatsapp-update-notes.replayDefence: none — last write wins on a notes field
whatsapp-update-notes.unauthorizedResponse: 401 missing authorization / invalid token, 403 not staff
whatsapp-update-notes.notes: Returns 500 when the is_staff() RPC errors rather than proceeding.

whatsapp-webhook.replayDefence: HMAC over the raw body; inbound events are deduplicated downstream by meta_message_id
whatsapp-webhook.unauthorizedResponse: 403 forbidden on a failed hub.verify_token handshake; 200 with the event stored as signature_valid=false and processing_status='failed' on a bad POST signature
whatsapp-webhook.emptySecretBehaviour: closed — an unset META_APP_SECRET produces a non-matching HMAC, so the request is logged and not processed
whatsapp-webhook.notes: The 200 on an invalid signature is deliberate: Meta retries non-2xx responses indefinitely. The request is NOT processed — it is recorded as a forensic trail and returns before any handling. Treat that 200 as a rejection, not an acceptance.

slack-alerts.caller: pg_cron (the 5-minute sweep and the 08:15 summary pair) and an AFTER INSERT trigger on booking_events, via pg_net
slack-alerts.replayDefence: none at the transport; a replayed call re-derives the same alert_key and is refused by the unique claim on slack_alerts
slack-alerts.emptySecretBehaviour: closed — !!WEBHOOK_SECRET guards the comparison, and isAuthorizedWebhook itself refuses an empty secret
slack-alerts.notes: #salon-today Slack alerts, dark-launched behind SLACK_ALERTS_ENABLED (default off) with a SLACK_ALERTS_DRY_RUN mode that logs instead of posting. Returns 200 on every failure path so a Slack outage cannot make pg_net retry or pg_cron log failures.
